ARMEE : RS 740.97 CR BONDADA EPC ORDER TERMINATED

• Company communicated inability to proceed with Bondada Engineering EPC project for NTPC Renewable Energy's Fatehgarh solar project (Block-1 and Block-3, 300 MW AC each)
• Aggregate order value was ₹740.97 Cr inclusive GST, comprising ₹375.18 Cr for Block-1 and ₹365.79 Cr for Block-3
• LOAs dated June 26, 2026 accepted earlier; contract price firm and fixed with no price escalation
• Substantial escalation in raw material costs made project commercially unviable
• Outstanding order book shall stand reduced by ₹740.97 Cr; other financial implications to be disclosed later
Impact: Negative (removes ~₹741 Cr order from RHP-disclosed order book, impacting near-term revenue visibility)

BSE , NSE ,BROKING STOCKS ; SEBI REVISES CLOSING AUCTION SESSION (CAS) & DERIVATIVES TRADING TIMINGS

• CAS Duration: 10 minutes, from 3:30 PM to 3:40 PM.

• 3:30–3:31 PM: Reference price calculation and transition to CAS.

• 3:31–3:36 PM: Market and limit order entry.

• 3:36–3:40 PM: Only limit orders permitted, with random closure between 3:38 PM and 3:40 PM.

• Post-Close Session: 3:50 PM to 4:00 PM.

• Index Derivatives: Trading until 3:45 PM, except expiring contracts, which close at 3:30 PM on expiry days.

• Stock Derivatives: Trading until 3:45 PM, including expiry days.

• Special Trading Days: CAS will also apply with the same 10-minute duration.

• Derivatives Settlement: Settlement price calculation methodology to be revised.

GODIGIT : FAIRFAX DECLARED STRATEGIC BUYER FOR 60.72% IDBI STAKE WORTH OVER RS 52,878 CR

• Fairfax (FFHL and FIH) declared "Strategic Buyer" for 60.72% equity stake in IDBI Bank via GoI strategic disinvestment
• Bid price INR 81 per share, total ~₹52,878 Cr (~US$5.6 billion), ~23% premium to IDBI book value as of June 30, 2026
• Fairfax proposes to contribute FFHL's interests in Go Digit Life Insurance and Go Digit General Insurance (Digit) and FIH's interest in IIFL Capital Services to IDBI Bank
• Contribution transactions subject to RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI approvals; no binding definitive agreements yet
• Fairfax expects no change in governance or management of Digit; Kamesh Goyal remains Founder and Chairman
Impact: Positive (Proposed contribution to IDBI Bank could significantly strengthen Digit's distribution footprint, though subject to regulatory approvals)

SKYWAYS : APPROVES RS 7 CR UAE STEP-DOWN UNIT, RS 11 CR VIETNAM GUARANTEE

• Board approved disinvestment of 40% stake in wholly owned subsidiary Avito Global Freight Private Limited to its Core Operating Team for ₹92.12 L
• After the transfer, Avito will cease to be wholly owned but remain a subsidiary; Skyways will retain 60% of paid-up equity capital
• Board approved Skyways and Avito Core Operating Team to invest up to ₹2 Cr in Avito in one or more tranches
• Avito to incorporate a wholly owned subsidiary in Masdar City Free Zone, Abu Dhabi, UAE, making it a step-down subsidiary of Skyways
• Subscription cost for the UAE entity up to ₹7 Cr in one or more tranches; Avito will hold 100% shareholding
• Board approved corporate guarantee to Techombank for Skyways SLS Logistik Company Limited (Vietnam) up to VND 30,000,000,000 (~₹11 Cr) for a bank guarantee to IATA
Impact: Positive (Expands international logistics footprint via UAE step-down unit and supports Vietnam subsidiary operations; guarantee adds contingent liability)

VRLLOG : REVISES BUYBACK RECORD DATE TO OCTOBER 22, 2026

SOUTH INDIAN BANK : ANNOUNCES SENIOR MANAGEMENT DESIGNATION CHANGES

Board approved senior management re-designations on operating and reporting structural changes.
Anto George T to be Executive Vice President & Chief Business Officer from November 01, 2026; also identified as Material Risk Taker per RBI guidelines.
Nandakumar G to head Banking Operations Group from October 16, 2026; Vijith S to be Head of Internal Audit; Rekha V R to be Chief of Internal Vigilance.
None of the personnel are related to any Directors of the Bank.

YES BANK BROKER NOTE

*YES BANK | SC upholds quashing of INR 84.15bn AT-1 write-off to meaningfully hit Capital/earnings*

*What happened*
• Supreme Court dismissed appeals by Yes Bank, RBI and GoI, upholding the Bombay HC order quashing the Mar-20 write-off of INR 84.15bn in AT-1 bonds post restructuring of Yes Bank.
• Bonds involved: INR 30bn (9.50% coupon) and INR 54.15bn (9.00% coupon).

*Potential liability*
• Scenario A – Principal only: INR 84.15bn.
• Scenario B – Principal + accrued coupons: ~INR 137.70bn.

*Impact on financials (FY26)*

1. Net worth
• Reported net worth stood at INR 510.62bn.
• Scenario A: INR 426.47bn, down 16.5%, with BVPS declining from INR 16.3 to ~INR 13.6.
• Scenario B: INR 372.92bn, down 27.0%, with BVPS declining to ~INR 11.9.

2. PAT
• Potential liability equals 2.4x / 4.0x FY26 PAT of INR 34.76bn under Scenarios A/B.
• If fully charged to P&L, FY26 would swing to a loss of ~INR 49.39bn / INR 102.94bn, respectively.

3. Loan growth
• Against FY26 net advances of INR 2,734.45bn, the liability amounts to 3.1% / 5.0% of the loan book under Scenarios A/B, respectively.

4. Capital adequacy
• Reported CET-1 / CRAR stood at 13.5% / 15.3%.
• Scenario A: CET-1 declines to ~10.9% (-257bps) and CRAR to ~12.7%.
• Scenario B: CET-1 declines to ~9.3% (-421bps) and CRAR to ~11.1%, below the 11.5% minimum CRAR requirement including CCB, potentially necessitating a capital raise.

5. If AT-1 bonds are reinstated
• Annual coupon outgo would be ~INR 7.72bn pre-tax and INR 5.87bn post-tax, equivalent to ~12.4% of FY27E PAT of INR 47.42bn.
• Reinstatement would restore AT-1 eligibility as Tier-1 capital, partly cushioning the capital adequacy impact.

*Valuation implications*
• At ~INR 18/share, the stock trades at ~1.1x reported FY26 P/BV.
• P/B rises to ~1.3x / 1.5x on adjusted book value under Scenarios A/B, respectively.

*Key monitorables*
• Settlement could involve cash payment, bond reinstatement or conversion into equity, with the latter potentially diluting shareholders.
• Past coupons remain uncertain given the non-cumulative and discretionary nature of AT-1 coupons. Principal-only repayment remains our base case.
• The accounting treatment (P&L versus reserves) will determine the reported earnings impact, although the net-worth hit remains.
• Settlement timelines, potential staggered payments and any review/curative petition remain key monitorables.

*Bottom line*
Under our base case, net worth could decline by 16.5%, with the liability equivalent to 2.4x FY26 PAT and CET-1 falling by ~257bps. The resulting capital hit could constrain lending capacity and delay RoE recovery. Clarity on the settlement mechanism and accounting treatment will be key. Currently, we have a sell rating on the stock.

The Supreme Court rejected Tiger Global’s claim to tax treaty benefits on capital gains arising from the Mauritius investment route.

Transactions undertaken primarily to avoid taxes may also face scrutiny under the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR).

The proposed relief could benefit foreign investors routing investments through Mauritius and other jurisdictions with tax treaties with India.

MOSL on Fairfax IDBI Bank buy-in - 

- The CCEA has approved the sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52900 Cr (₹81/share), comprising 30.48% held by GoI and 30.24% by LIC.
- This is the biggest strategic disinvestment and will be the largest FDI in India’s financial sector to date
- GoI and LIC shall retain ~15% and ~19% stake, respectively, but will have no Board representation, which makes IDBI Bank a Promoter-led private bank. 
- Fairfax will have to make an open offer to minority shareholders after the share purchase agreement is signed. The terms aren’t public yet.
- Fairfax will have a five-year lock-in and a 15-year      glide path to bring its stake down to 26%. It should also merge or exit its ~40% stake in CSB Bank within two years.

We present below a snapshot of how the numbers for the merged entity will look should Fairfax decide to merge the two banks (IDBI Bank + CSB Bank)–

Balance sheet size: The balance sheet size shall increase by 13.1% with total assets increasing to INR5t.
Gold book mix post-merger: CSB’s Gold book mix is 54% of its overall book and stands at INR 219b. The acquisition shall lead to the Gold book increasing from 9% currently for IDBI to ~15% of the total merged entity loan book.
CD ratio: The C/D ratio post-acquisition for IDBI shall increase marginally to 80.6% from 79.5%, given CSB’s CD ratio is at 88.8% as on Jun-26.
Employee base: IDBI Bank has a higher employee base at 20,123 vs 8,187 for CSB Bank, taking the combined base to ~28,310.
Branch count: IDBI Bank has 2,243 branches vs 862 for CSB Bank, taking the combined network to ~3,105 branches.
CASA mix & Cost of Funds: IDBI Bank's CASA ratio is higher at 43.6% vs 19.4% for CSB Bank, resulting in a combined CASA of      ~40.7%. Cost of funds stands at 4.7% for IDBI vs 6.6% for CSB.
NIMs: IDBI Bank's NIM stands at 3.61% vs 3.66% for CSB Bank, implying a broadly neutral impact on the combined entity's NIM at ~3.6%. CSB's gold loan-heavy portfolio (54% of advances) supports yields.
Opex: IDBI Bank's C/I ratio is lower at 52.0% vs 64.6% for CSB Bank, with the combined ratio at ~54.6%, offering scope for operating efficiencies.
Credit costs & Asset quality: IDBI Bank's credit cost stood at -1.1% vs 0.5% for CSB Bank. GNPA/NNPA      stood at 2.3%/0.2% for IDBI and 1.8%/0.4% for CSB.
RoA/RoE: IDBI Bank reported RoA/RoE of 2.2%/14.6% in FY26 vs 1.2%/12.9% for CSB Bank.
BVPS and valuations: The BVPS of CSB is INR 289 as against INR 64.8 of IDBI. P/B on a trailing basis for both the entities stands at 1.1x and 1.4x currently.

MRPL has delivered a blockbuster Q2 but the numbers need some context.

Revenue rose 37% YoY to ₹35,590 Cr, while EBITDA more than doubled to ₹3,210 Cr. PAT surged 194% to ₹1,881 Cr.

The interesting part? Refinery throughput actually declined from 4.43 MMT to 4.18 MMT.

So, the earnings jump was not driven by higher volumes. Elevated crude and product prices lifted the reported topline, while the rising-price environment likely aided inventory valuation and refining profitability.

EBITDA margin consequently expanded from 6.0% to 9.0%.

However, MRPL has not separately disclosed its GRM or inventory gain in this release so the entire quarterly profit should not be treated as a steady-state run rate.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now

ELECON ENGINEERING - NAVAL PROPULSION GEARBOXES

BUSINESS OVERVIEW
- Elecon is a major industrial gear solutions provider.
- Naval propulsion gearboxes represent a specialised defence opportunity.
- Gearboxes reduce turbine speed and increase torque.
- They transfer power to warship propeller shafts.

TWO KEY GEARBOX TYPES
- COGAG: Two gas turbines combine power through one gearbox.
- COGAG supports high-speed propulsion.
- This system powers INS Vikrant.
- CODOG: Uses diesel for cruising and gas turbines for speed.
- Gearboxes switch between the two power sources.
- Elecon has delivered 14 units for the Navy's stealth fleet.

WHY ENTRY BARRIERS ARE HIGH
- Gearboxes handle enormous power with minimal failure tolerance.
- Low noise and vibration support stealth requirements.
- Equipment must withstand underwater explosion shock.
- Design, testing and Navy trials take years.
- Qualification limits the number of eligible suppliers.

STRATEGIC ADVANTAGES
- Qualified suppliers face limited competition in tenders.
- Warships require spares and overhauls throughout their lifecycles.
- Indigenous manufacturing supports defence import substitution.
- INS Vikrant provides an important reference project.
- Existing projects could support future naval programme opportunities.

ORDER BOOK AND PIPELINE
- Q2 open order book increased 33.4%.
- Current growth is mainly driven by the MHE division.
- Naval opportunities worth approximately ₹1,000 Cr are at RFP stage.
- Potential orders may enter the order book around Q4.
- Conversion of the pipeline remains a key monitorable.

KEY MONITORABLES
- Conversion of naval RFPs into firm orders.
- Contribution of defence orders to the order book.
- Execution of existing naval gearbox programmes.
- Future frigate, destroyer and carrier opportunities.
- Revenue from lifecycle spares and overhauls.

INVESTMENT UNDERSTANDING
- Naval gearboxes offer a specialised defence opportunity.
- Qualification creates potentially durable competitive advantages.
- Long warship lifecycles may support aftermarket revenue.
- The ₹1,000 Cr pipeline remains unconverted.
- Current order-book growth mainly reflects the MHE division.

*KEY TAKEAWAYS: CONCALL BY MR. RAAMDEO AGARWAL*
*Motilal Oswal Wealth Management | 10th Oct 2026*

*MARKET AT RARE VALUATION OPPORTUNITY - TIME TO DOUBLE UP, NOT SELL*

*1. Valuation is at multi-year low - 18% discount to average*
Nifty is currently trading at *17.2x 12-month forward P/E*, vs its 10-year average of *20.9x*. This is an *18% discount to Long Period Average*.
This is the same level we saw in COVID crash of 2020.
From the Sep'24 peak, valuations have cooled sharply:
*Nifty-50: 24.8x -> 17.2x (-31%)*
Midcap-150: 35.6x -> 22.8x (-36%)
Smallcap-250: 25.0x -> 23.2x (-7%)

*2. A unique situation in history*
For the *first time ever*, Indian Economy is doing well BUT Markets are at 52-week low and giving *negative returns in last 2 years*.
We remain the *Fastest Growing Economy, but the Worst Performing Stock Market* in the world. This gap will not last long.

*3. All headwinds are already priced in*
Market has already absorbed everything together:
Higher Crude Oil prices, Depreciating INR, Rising Bond Yields, Super El Nino.
Despite all this, our earnings engine is intact.

*4. Earnings have started to show - 20-25% growth expected*
Nifty 2Q earnings expected at *Sales +17% / PAT +27% YoY*.
MOFSL Universe PAT growth to hit an *11-quarter high of 22%*.
This is a broad-based recovery - for the first time in years, *almost every sector is expected to grow.*
Key contributors: *Cement (+35%), EMS (+34%), Retail (+22%), Consumer Durables (+20%)*
Auto volumes up >30%, Bank credit growth at decade high.
Markets are trading at *PEG < 1* - meaning you are paying less than earnings growth. Very attractive.

*5. Our Top Picks across Sectors*
*Large caps*
Reliance, LT, bharti, sbi, hdfcbank, kotak,tcs & infy,adaniports,adani power, adani enterprise
*Midcaps*
Trent,idea,Fluorochem,Cummins, ENRIN,GVTD, Kirloskar Oil, , Syrma SGS, MTAR, Divi Labs, Laurus Labs, Rubicon Research,  Shaily Engg, MolBio Diagnostics, Pearl Global, Welspun Living, Navin Fluorine,  Samvardhana Motherson, sonacoms,eternal, paytm,lenskart
*Small caps*
Aequs, marine, paragmilk,fredun pharma, one source, senoras pharma, samman capital, dynamatic technology,kwality walls,sasken technology,sudarshan chemical

*6. What can trigger the sharp reversal?*
US Bond Yield normally peaks at *5.3% to 5.5%* and appears to be in an overbought zone. Similarly, USDINR also looks to be peaking at these levels.
If there is any positive news on the war front and Crude cools off to *$60*, we will see a massive correction in Bond Yields and appreciation in INR.
That will be a powerful trigger for markets to re-rate sharply from these depressed valuations.

*CONCLUSION:*
In 2024, Nifty traded at 25 PE. Today it is at *31% discount* to that peak, while earnings have started to revive.
In worst of times, we get the best of opportunity.

This is not the time to sell in panic. *This is the time to double up investments and accumulate quality. Don't miss this opportunity.*

**BROKER VIEW**
- Rating: REDUCE (Downgraded from HOLD).
- Target Price: ₹3,214.
- Previous Target Price: ₹4,027.
- Brokerage: Prabhudas Lilladher.

**KEY CONCERNS**

**1. Quick Commerce Competition**
- Competition from quick-commerce players is intensifying.
- Online grocery shifts pressure growth and margins.
- Commodity inflation remains difficult to pass on.

**2. Weak Store Productivity**
- Sales per store and square foot remain subdued.
- Bills per store per day declined 4.1% YoY.
- New store clusters are diluting overall throughput.
- Added 15 stores in Q2FY27.
- Total store count reached 518.

**3. DMart Ready Limitations**
- Online platform currently operates in 11 cities.
- Expansion strategy faces fast-changing competitive dynamics.
- Quick-commerce competition remains a key challenge.

**Q2FY27 PERFORMANCE**
- Results missed estimates.
- Lower gross margins pressured profitability.
- Higher interest costs and lower other income added pressure.

**MARGIN OUTLOOK**
- FY26 EBITDA margin: 7.5%.
- FY28E EBITDA margin: 7.1%.
- FY29E EBITDA margin: 7.0%.
- Limited pricing power may constrain margin recovery.

**ESTIMATE REVISIONS**
- FY28E estimates cut by 3.2%.
- FY29E estimates cut by 4.4%.
- FY26–29E EPS CAGR projected at 13.2%.

**VALUATION CONCERNS**
- FY28E P/E: approximately 61x.
- FY29E P/E: approximately 53.3x.
- ROE declined from 16.5% in FY23 to 12.8%.
- Rich valuations leave limited room for disappointments.

**KEY MONITORABLES**
- Quick-commerce competition and market-share trends.
- Sales per store and square-foot productivity.
- Gross margins and operating cost trends.
- New-store profitability and throughput improvement.
- ROE recovery and valuation comfort.

**INVESTMENT TAKEAWAY**
Store expansion continues, but productivity remains under pressure.
Quick commerce challenges pricing power and growth.
Margins and ROE face further pressure.
High valuations increase downside sensitivity.

**NO RECOMMENDATION**

JPMORGAN ON RBI

KEY TAKEAWAYS

RBI has announced a special window to meet the USD requirements of public sector OMCS

This effectively removes a large part of $12bn/month net oil import dollar demand from the onshore FX market, equivalent to ~16% of the total goods import bill

To suck out further liquidity, the RBI announced OMO sales of Rs 25000 cr and raised the minimum daily maintenance of the CRR to 99% from 90%

These measures would suck out Rs 50000 cr of durable liquidity from the system

Banking-system liquidity is likely to tighten in the coming days, which should move money market rates closer to the policy rate

JEFFERIES ON BANKS

KEY TAKEAWAYS

RBI Tightens Daily CRR; Small Impact on NIM, to Flow Through to NBFCs/ Corps

In line with the change in MPC stance to 'calibrated tightening', RBI raised daily CRR from 90% to 99%

Banks need to fully meet full CRR norm of 3% of NDTL

At 100% CRR, banks would carry Rs 8 lakh cr in CRR

If this lifts balances by 5-10%, it can withdraw Rs400-800bn of liquidity & add 1-2 bps to cost of funds

It is a small dilution of NIMs & banks may be able to pass to borrowers

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.

Is India investing enough for future capacity

India is usually described as a consumption economy. Consumption contributes >60% of GDP. But the story becomes incomplete when we ignore what's happening on the investment side and other aspects of our economy

India's Gross Capital Formation is ~32.6% of GDP. Lower than China's ~40%, but China's per capita GDP is several times of India's. Comparing ratios without considering income levels misses the context.

A developing country cannot allocate every ₹ toward factories & infra. A large share of resources must also support the bottom of the pyramid through housing, healthcare, education & welfare.

A harmonious society requires a minimum standard of living for those at the bottom. India is building capacity while simultaneously funding social stability. That's a tougher balancing act than many realize.

So let's move beyond GDP narratives & look at hard physical data. India's share of global GDP is only ~3.5% yet produces roughly 10% of the world's steel. Steel almost 3x our weight in global GDP. Steel isn't consumed for consumption's sake, but goes into factories, rail tracks, power plants, ports, airports, infrastructure etc

Cement tells the same story. India produces ~400 MT annually out of ~4,000 MT globally. Again, roughly 10% global share despite only ~3.5% share of world GDP. Countries don't consume steel & cement at this scale unless they are building physical assets. These are the raw materials of future GDP.

Power generation presents a slightly different picture. India's share of global electricity output is lower than steel & cement, but still materially ahead of its global GDP share. India with 1800bn units vs 32,000bn units, 6% global share

The evidence suggests India is investing for future capability. One may argue the investment cycle started later than it should have, but the direction is unmistakable. Steel, Cement & Power share point toward economy preparing for a much larger future.

The scale of projects are also changing. DFCs, industrial corridors, semiconductor fabs, renewable energy parks, metros, airports, transmission corridors & logistics networks are larger than anything India attempted before.

If this trend continues, India's share of global steel, cement & power usage is likely to keep rising. Higher material intensity today is often a precursor to higher economic output tomorrow.

Maybe the better way to describe India isn't "consumption economy." It's a country simultaneously consuming, uplifting millions & building future productive capacity. 
India need a balancing act of Building future and taking care of the needy, which it is working towards

De-Dollarization lets peek into central bank reserves

Central banks are diversifying but US$ isn't giving up the throne anytime soon. Headlines scream de-dollarization bt US$ still makes up ~57% of global FX reserves. That's down from decades ago, but still miles ahead of everyone else.

Euro is the 2nd largest reserve currency at ~20%. But Europe faces weak growth, aging demographics, fiscal stress & fragmented politics. Hence no comfort for people looking to diversify away from US$

Then its China. Despite its economic size, RMB is only ~2% of global reserves & ~2% of global payments. Clear reflection of trust issues with the dragon. deep capital markets, convertibility & rule of law issues also there

They're moving into something with no issuer at all: Gold. Central banks themselves are now one of the biggest sources of gold demand globally, roughly buy ~30% of annual global mine production

Gold isn't rising only because investors are bullish. Significant chunk of global prodn is locked away by sovereign balance sheets. In 2026, central banks gold buying at slower pace vs 2025 due to 60% price rise.

Among the Major buyers were Poland, China, Brazil, India etc. 
Then there are few sellers too. Turkey has been among the largest sellers this year, reportedly selling ~83t YTD to support liquidity & FX/US$ needs.

That’s the problem. Though world want to move away from US$ in the long term but  issue in the medium term created due to lack of US$ in the country. 
Case in point Turkiye

Russia has also been a notable seller, reducing reserves by ~44t YTD as it seeks hard-currency liquidity. But Russia is also large producer of Gold

Gold is becoming a reserve diversification asset in a world where trust in fiat issuers is fragmenting.
BUT de-dollarization in reserves doesn't mean de-dollarization in trade.
That’s two very different thing

Global trade still run on the USD infrastructure. That network effect is incredibly hard to replace.
So its two-step process. Trade continues in USD.
But exporting nations convert a portion of their accumulated surplus reserves into gold, commodities, sovereign funds or other reserve assets.

The world may keep transacting in dollars while increasingly choosing not to store all its savings in dollars.

Conclusion:
Real story is different from "the end of the USD."
Reserve diversification is real.
Dollar replacement is not. Not in near future
